message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). For selecting a best-supported direct-match, PGS000753 stands out as the most disease-focused AAA-specific study (Million Veteran Program AAA architecture paper) and it reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD = 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which provides direct evidence of PRS signal without relying on full-model AUROC. Competing models either come from framework/benchmarking contexts with metrics that are likely full-model or otherwise not clearly PRS-only (e.g., PGS001784 reports AUROC=0.868 but with extensive covariates and only a small covariates-regressed-out R2=0.0147; PGS002054 is from a portability framework with partial-r=0.0144; PGS003429/PGS003972 report modest full-model AUROC ~0.69–0.71 with unknown covariates; PGS003973 reports a high C-index=0.882 but it is not clearly PRS-only and includes age/sex terms). Limitation: across the pool, PRS-only AUROC is not provided and several reported discrimination metrics appear to be full-model, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain; therefore confidence is moderate and the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches for the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder): PGS002738 and PGS002739 have trait_efo='alcohol dependence' with phenotyping_reported='Alcohol use disorder', while PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled 'Problematic alcohol use' but use an AUD DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype (still closely aligned). Among these, PGS002738 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (explicit AUD with alcohol dependence EFO), disease-focused multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB), and the strongest visible discrimination-style evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900). However, the overall evidence remains limited for a high-confidence pick because none of the models report PRS-only AUROC or PRS-only R2, covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and the two UKB-based DSM-5-count scores report only small incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) that are not directly comparable to the OR metric. These gaps prevent a clearly high-quality direct-match designation despite PGS002738 being the most coherent choice from the available metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder), but the evidence is limited by lack of PRS-comparable AUC/R2 across the set (no PGS-only AUROC; only incremental/other metrics or top-decile ORs). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches in concept, but two (PGS002738, PGS002739) are the most endpoint-faithful to the target because they report trait_efo=\"alcohol dependence\" and phenotyping_reported=\"Alcohol use disorder\" (a direct clinical endpoint), whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled \"Problematic alcohol use\" with trait_efo=\"alcohol dependence measurement\" despite using an AUD DSM-5 criteria count phenotype. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/AUD), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and the strength/clarity of PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS002738 is the best-supported direct-match because its trait fields align exactly with the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and it reports a reasonably strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900) with development cohorts listed as MVP and UKB, suggesting a more disease-focused multi-cohort basis than the UKB-only siblings. The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2, and PGS002738 has unknown covariates, reducing comparability and preventing a high-confidence selection. The two UKB-based ‘Problematic alcohol use’ models (PGS000201/PGS000202) have DSM-5 AUD criteria-count phenotyping (still relevant) and report small ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456), but they are conceptually one step removed from a binary AUD diagnosis label and show weaker incremental variance explained than the OR evidence in PGS002738. PGS002739 is direct for AUD but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples and uses a gene-based PRS-CSx approach with a very small feature set (858), making it less generally supported than PGS002738 given the context provided."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001777","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis. PGS001777 is the most disease-focused and endpoint-relevant in the visible metadata (publication explicitly about alcohol-related cirrhosis risk in drinkers; trait_reported aligns; reports a strong risk gradient: OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18 [4.05–9.41]). However, the evidence is not cleanly decisive because (i) its selected AUROC=0.671 is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUC/R2 provided), (ii) covariates are listed as Unknown, and (iii) validation sample size is small (n=1,390). Competing models have different strengths but also key limitations: PGS000704 has a larger validation set and basic covariates but appears to be a UKB biomarker/pan-trait framework-style model with only full-model C-index=0.711 and modest HR=1.18 per SD; PGS004913 is disease-focused and phenotype-aligned but reports only a small R²=0.029 (not explicitly PGS-only) and has wide OR uncertainty. Given these tradeoffs and lack of PRS-only comparable metrics across the set, selection remains sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris), spanning several endpoint instantiations (generic angina, ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, and time-to-event). Among models with clearly PRS-comparable metrics, the UKB snpnet family (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) reports PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.59) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014; liability h2 ~0.134), avoiding obvious metric inflation. PGS001262 is preferred within this family because it has the strongest incremental signal (incremental AUROC 0.0098) and the highest full-model AUROC (0.807) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and it uses a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint. Limitation: these snpnet scores come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (‘across 813 traits’), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; competing newer ICD10/PheCode models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527 and PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057) report only full-model C-index or per-SD OR without clear PGS-only metrics/covariates, making them hard to compare directly and preventing a high-confidence, clearly best-supported choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned endpoints (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3 variants). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet pan-trait UKB framework siblings (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014; liability h2 ~0.134), while several newer ICD10/PheCode models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527) lack PRS-only discrimination metrics and provide only per-SD ORs, and the MVP benchmarking set (PGS005047–PGS005059) reports C-index/full-model metrics and ORs but does not clearly provide PRS-only AUC/R2 in the visible fields. Within the snpnet trio, PGS001262 has the strongest reported full-model AUROC (0.80729) and the highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) with similar basic covariates and a directly stated doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype, making it the best-supported choice from the available evidence.
